localChanges: chore: update core-city, civ1-city-improvement and civ1-wonder

log: Build (civ-clone/web-renderer#292, from the production menu, F0_1ade_0421): Hydro and Nuclear Plants no longer need a Factory, a Mfg. Plant needs only Robotics, and a Factory isn't offered once the city has a Mfg. Plant.

Yields (civ-clone/web-renderer#390, from CityWorker.cs): Library and University each add half of the base science (core-city's new base argument) rather than of the running total. Shields follow v474.05's factory/plant factors: a Factory adds 2/4 of base and a Mfg. Plant 4/4 in its place; a plant adds 2/4, only with a Factory or Mfg. Plant, and plants don't stack. Marketplace, Bank and Courthouse are unchanged (they compound in v474.05 too).
The build priority wants a plant in a city with a Mfg. Plant as well as one with a Factory.
Needs core-city with YieldModifier's base argument.
chore: require core-city 0.1.23, which passes YieldModifiers the base yields

From CityWorker.cs (civ-clone/web-renderer#390): Isaac Newton's College adds a third of the base science per Library and University (was a x11/9 multiplier per improvement). Copernicus doubles the city's science and SETI adds half (now floored), both after every Low modifier, so they act on the Library/University/Newton total whatever order the packages register in. Hoover Dam adds half of the base shields.

From the production menu (civ-clone/web-renderer#292): a city on the continent of its player's Hoover Dam isn't offered a Power, Hydro or Nuclear Plant. cityBuild takes the LandMassRegistry for this; registerRules passes game.landMasses.
Needs core-city with YieldModifier's base argument.
chore: require core-city 0.1.23, which passes YieldModifiers the base yields

City.yields() now runs the YieldRules, snapshots what they produced, and hands that snapshot to every YieldModifier as a third argument, after the running total. A modifier that adds a share of the base (a Library's +50% in Civ1) can read it, so it doesn't compound on another modifier's output or depend on the order the packages register their rules in. Existing modifiers ignore the extra argument.
